goal: Overnight recipe search for a season-long trajectory model producing FluSight's peak targets (peak week probabilities over the 34 window weeks, peak incidence quantiles), organized as a tree (user delegation 2026-10-12).
training_problem: problems/us-flu-long-horizon.json: flu admissions and ED, weeks 1-36 ahead, finalized histories and labels, leave-one-season-out 2023-24/2024-25/2025-26 (each fold trains on the other three of 2022-23..2025-26).
evaluation_problem: problems/us-flu-season-peak.json, scored with chromantis.seasonal (model=trajectory, 512 draws pooled over the recipe's seeds) at every Saturday reference date in the window (epiweeks 40-21), finalized history through the previous week, truth = finalized NHSN.
selection_score: States/DC mean over reference dates before the true peak of: peak-week negative log score (probability floored at 0.001) + peak-incidence WIS on log(1 + admissions). Lower is better. Both terms reported separately, plus US and the 8+ / 0-7 weeks-before-peak splits.
references: Past FluSight peak submissions (2024-25: 7 models, 2025-26: 12 models) imported with chromantis.seasonal.import_hub and scored on their own submitted tasks (states/DC, reference dates before the true peak); our models are scored on exactly those tasks. Hub forecasts were real-time from reported data; ours start from finalized history; truth is finalized NHSN.
expansion_rule: A child is better than its parent only if its selection score is lower by more than the seed noise (estimated from per-seed trajectory scores of the round).
Each round expands the two best recipes plus at most one uncertain recipe; a setting that hurts in two rounds is dropped.
One fit per GPU (36-week sampled fits reach about 28 GB); about 6 concurrent fits.
Every round is a planner experiment season-peak-tree-rNN with its study file round-NN.json; decisions appended below with their numbers.
No commits, pushes, production or release changes; stop and leave a note on any failure other than GPU memory.
policy: Claude decides each expansion between rounds by the rule above (user delegation 2026-10-12); the user may intervene at any time.
decisions: 2026-10-12: root = the stage-2b recipes (season-peak-stage2b): 36-week sampled A-family MLP with path loss (energy score of log(1 + admissions) paths) and peak loss (fair CRPS of path peak size and soft peak week). Three-seed early read of path+peak weight 1: peak week 2.93 (8+ weeks before peak, states/DC) vs climatology 3.33 and uniform 3.53; peak size log WIS 1.06 vs climatology 0.47 (median predicted/true peak size 0.71).

2026-10-12, benchmark against past FluSight peak submissions (user request), states/DC, dates before the true peak, each Hub model's own tasks (mostly from November-December on). Peak week (-log probability): FluSight-ensemble 2.57 vs path+peak (3 seeds) 2.98, climatology 3.75, recursive Bes 3.48 (897 cells, 2024-25 and 2025-26); best Hub models 2.22 (UGA Scenariocast), 2.32 (NAU vulPES, PSI-PROF_beta), CU-ensemble 2.53 vs our 2.69 on its tasks. Peak size (log WIS): FluSight-ensemble 0.53 vs path+peak 0.33, recursive Bes 0.25, climatology 0.45; our size advantage is partly finalized inputs. Target for the tree: peak week at or below the FluSight-ensemble's on its tasks, keeping peak size below it.
